FROMLIST: rtw88: configure firmware after HCI started After firmware has been downloaded, driver should send some information to it through H2C commands. Those H2C commands are transmitted through TX path. But before HCI has been started, the TX path is not working completely. Such as PCI interfaces, the interrupts are not enabled, hence TX interrupts will not be issued after H2C skb has been DMAed to the device. And the H2C skbs will not be released until the device is powered off. Signed-off-by: Yan-Hsuan Chuang <yhchuang@realtek.com> (am from https://patchwork.kernel.org/patch/11146411/) (also found at https://lkml.kernel.org/r/1568617425-28062-3-git-send-email-yhchuang@realtek.com) BUG=b:124400293 BUG=b:140070313 TEST=none Change-Id: I34505dfe860a80029856dcac80c5386d644ca99d Signed-off-by: Yan-Hsuan Chuang <yhchuang@realtek.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1775692 Tested-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org>

FROMLIST: rtw88: pci: reset H2C queue indexes in a single write If the driver doesn't reset the host's and device's indexes in a single write, the indexes will become different in a short period. And it will confuse the DMA engine, make it start to process non-existed entries. Better to Write-1-to-reset the indexes, for the DMA engine to know that this is a reset of the H2C queue, not a kick off. Signed-off-by: Yan-Hsuan Chuang <yhchuang@realtek.com> (am from https://patchwork.kernel.org/patch/11146419/) (also found at https://lkml.kernel.org/r/1568617425-28062-4-git-send-email-yhchuang@realtek.com) BUG=b:124400293 TEST=see if there's any DMA error Change-Id: Ib2f4904f0533351737b534f54375e228e2356b10 Signed-off-by: Yan-Hsuan Chuang <yhchuang@realtek.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1775693 Tested-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org>

FROMLIST: rtw88: pci: release tx skbs DMAed when stop Interrupt is disabled to stop PCI, which means the skbs queued for each TX ring will not be released via DMA interrupt. To avoid those skbs remained being left in the skb queue until PCI has been removed, driver needs to release skbs by itself. Signed-off-by: Yan-Hsuan Chuang <yhchuang@realtek.com> (am from https://patchwork.kernel.org/patch/11146417/) (also found at https://lkml.kernel.org/r/1568617425-28062-6-git-send-email-yhchuang@realtek.com) BUG=b:124400293 BUG=b:140070313 TEST=none Change-Id: I424dd0b93fc38f674255a27f2db620b8b84fb58a Signed-off-by: Yan-Hsuan Chuang <yhchuang@realtek.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1710448 Tested-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org>

libchromeos-ui: Add video_capture_use_gpu_memory_buffer USE flag The --video-capture-use-gpu-memory-buffer switch controls whether the video capture stack on Chrome uses GpuMemoryBuffer as frame buffers. On Chrome OS, using GpuMemoryBuffer backed with DMA-buf buffers allows us to eliminate significant numbers of buffer copies on the CPU, achieving zero-copy on the CPU for most camera use cases. BUG=chromium:982201 TEST=Build and deploy libchromeos-ui to DUT. Verify that the switch is added to Chrome args when video_capture_use_gpu_memory_buffer is present in /etc/ui_use_flags.txt. Change-Id: Iaa405ccf0b91d7ff380487377fb3656680217045 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1827100 Tested-by: Ricky Liang <jcliang@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Ricky Liang <jcliang@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Ricky Liang <jcliang@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mattias Nissler <mnissler@chromium.org>
